subject: current_process
statement: Today HR collects onboarding data via a Word document and an Excel file and then types everything into the receiving parties' portals by hand; last month two new hires took a full afternoon.

anchors.quote: I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand.
Last month I spent a full afternoon on two new hires.

subject: hiring_volume
statement: Muster AG hires around twenty people a year (more in summer) and has about 150 employees, mostly in Zurich.

anchors.quote: Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.

subject: source_tax_pain
statement: Source tax is HR's biggest time sink: HR does not know up front who must answer the source tax questions, so the whole questionnaire is sent to everybody and Swiss employees get annoyed and call.

anchors.quote: Source tax, without any doubt.
So I send the whole questionnaire to everybody, and the Swiss people get annoyed, and they call me.

subject: source_tax_questions
statement: Source tax questions should only be asked to employees who are subject to source tax, not to everybody.

anchors.quote: Because I never know up front who has to answer those questions.
So who actually needs to answer them?

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Initial statement: all non-Swiss employees (anyone without a Swiss passport) are subject to source tax.

anchors.quote: All the non-Swiss employees. Simple as that. If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: The Zurich source tax calculator (canton website, yields the tariff code) is used for every employee, regardless of where they live; HR acknowledges this is not exactly how it works but it is the approach for now, and Leo agreed to keep it.

anchors.quote: For everybody I use Zurich, by the way. I know it's not exactly how it works, but that's what we do for now.
Understood. We'll keep that for now.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: Today HR sits with the employee's answers and clicks through the Zurich calculator, which gives the tariff code.

anchors.quote: The one that gives you the tariff code. I sit with the answers and click through it.

subject: address
statement: HR needs the employee's home address.

anchors.quote: Yes, I need the address, obviously.

subject: address
statement: The address must be complete: street, house number, postcode, town and country, because HR posts many documents to employees.

anchors.quote: The full address. Street, number, postcode, town, country. We post a lot of documents to people, so it has to be complete.

subject: address
statement: Nothing beyond a normal postal address is needed: the address as one would write it on an envelope.

anchors.quote: No, no. Just a normal address, the way you would write it on an envelope.

subject: photo
statement: HR would like the form to ask for a photo of the employee for badges (currently reception takes poor phone pictures).

anchors.quote: Could the form ask for a photo?
For the badges.

subject: photo
statement: No photo is collected for now; security is changing the badge system next year and the topic is postponed to next year.

anchors.quote: Let's not do that now. Forget the photo for the moment, we'll talk about it next year.
Okay, no photo.

subject: pension_fund
statement: Muster AG's pension fund is Pensionskasse Muster, which has an old portal; Anna will send screenshots of it.

anchors.quote: We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call

subject: first_working_day
statement: The employee's first working day is needed for the pension fund; it is the most important item.

anchors.quote: I need their first working day. That's the number one thing

subject: first_working_day
statement: The employee should confirm the first working day, because it changes often (e.g. people negotiate an earlier exit with their old employer).

anchors.quote: I ask them to confirm it, because it moves more often than you'd think.
People negotiate with their old employer, they get out a week earlier.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Pension fund insurance starts on the first of the month following the first working day (e.g. first working day 15 March → insurance start 1 April).

anchors.quote: because insurance starts on the first of the following month. So for her that was the first of April

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Exception: if the first working day is exactly the first of a month, insurance starts on that day.

anchors.quote: Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Consolidated: insurance start date is derived from the (latest confirmed) first working day: if it is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month.

anchors.quote: because insurance starts on the first of the following month.
Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day.

subject: first_working_day
statement: Incident: Julia moved her first working day to 15 March, HR did not update it, the fund had a wrong insurance start date, leading to an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing. This implies the insurance start date must follow changes to the first working day.

anchors.quote: She moved her first working day to the 15th of March, and I didn't update it.
It took weeks to fix.

subject: civil_status
statement: The pension fund asks for the employee's civil status.

anchors.quote: Yes, the civil status. They ask for that.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: If the employee is married, the pension fund wants the date of birth of the husband or wife.

anchors.quote: And if someone is married, they want the date of birth of the husband or wife.

subject: civil_status
statement: Civil status options per Anna's recollection (hedged, to be verified against the screenshots): Single, married, divorced, and she thinks widowed.

anchors.quote: I'd have to look. You'll see it in the screenshots. Single, married, divorced, I think widowed.

subject: civil_status
statement: Muster AG has at least one employee (Daniel, finance) in a registered partnership.

anchors.quote: we do have one colleague in a registered partnership. Daniel, in finance.

subject: civil_status
statement: Unknown how the pension fund screen handles a registered partnership and whether the fund wants the partner's details too.

anchors.quote: I honestly don't know what the fund's screen does in that case, or if they want the partner's details too.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Correction: non-Swiss employees with a C permit are not subject to source tax; they are treated like Swiss people for this.

anchors.quote: No, that's actually not right.
So, not the people with a C permit. They're treated like Swiss people for this.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Leo summarised 'non-Swiss, but not with a C permit'; Anna only hedged ('I think so') and later added further cases.

anchors.quote: Okay, so non-Swiss, but not with a C permit. Is that everything?
I think so.

subject: source_tax_effort
statement: Anna offered to get numbers from the payroll person on how long source tax processing takes.

anchors.quote: I could get that for you from our payroll person.

subject: it_equipment
statement: Laptops/IT equipment are out of scope; IT has its own process.

anchors.quote: IT does laptops, they have their own process, keep them out of this, please.

subject: permit_reminder
statement: HR would love the form to remind people to bring their permit on the first day; not decided (wording to be looked at later).

anchors.quote: What I would love is if the form could remind people to bring their permit. Half of them forget.
We can look at the wording later.

subject: spouse_employment
statement: For married employees, the source tax calculator asks additional questions, e.g. whether the husband or wife works.

anchors.quote: It changes the questions in the calculator, yes. Whether the husband or wife works.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: An employee married to someone Swiss or to someone with a C permit, where that spouse lives in Switzerland, is not subject to source tax (e.g. Tomás: Brazilian, B permit, Swiss wife, living in Winterthur → no source tax).

anchors.quote: If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
Brazilian, B permit, but his wife is Swiss, and they live in Winterthur. So no source tax for him.

subject: spouse_details
statement: For married employees, the spouse's nationality, permit (if any) and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland are needed to determine source tax liability.

anchors.quote: So you need to know about the spouse as well.
Yes. Their nationality, their permit if they have one, and that they live here.

subject: spouse_details
statement: Today HR checks the spouse case by hand and asks for spouse details by email, which takes forever.

anchors.quote: I always have to check that one by hand.
I ask them by email, and it takes forever.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Employees who work in Switzerland but live abroad (e.g. Konstanz in Germany, Liechtenstein) are always subject to source tax, regardless of nationality – even Swiss citizens.

anchors.quote: Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here. And there it doesn't matter what passport you have, by the way.
Stefan is actually Swiss, and he still has it.
So someone living abroad and working here always does it?
Yes.

subject: cross_border_source_tax
statement: For employees living abroad the source tax calculator has many more questions; Germany has its own forms whose names Anna cannot recall. Leo noted the calculator will tell which questions apply.

anchors.quote: And with them the calculator gets much more complicated, there are more questions. Germany has its own forms, I can never remember what they're called.
Okay, that's fine, the calculator will tell us.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Consolidated final rule: an employee is subject to source tax if they live abroad (home address country not Switzerland), regardless of nationality. If they live in Switzerland, they are subject only if they are not Swiss and do not hold a C permit, unless they are married to a spouse who is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland (then not subject).

anchors.quote: If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.
So, not the people with a C permit.
If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.

subject: nationality
statement: The employee's nationality is needed to determine source tax liability.

anchors.quote: If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.

subject: permit_type
statement: For non-Swiss employees, the permit type (e.g. C permit vs B permit) is needed to determine source tax liability.

anchors.quote: So, not the people with a C permit.
Brazilian, B permit

subject: address_country
statement: Whether the employee lives abroad can be derived from the country of the home address, which is relevant for source tax liability.

anchors.quote: Street, number, postcode, town, country.
Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.

subject: project_timing
statement: Anna asked about timing; Leo will respond this week after reviewing the screenshots.

anchors.quote: Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
